C-TOOLBAR-LABELS.Name: Retain visited inline toolbar labels until the pointer leaves the whole panel
C-TOOLBAR-LABELS.Summary: Prevent corner toolbars from shrinking and moving between adjacent buttons. Each visited button keeps its inline label open while the pointer remains in that toolbar; leaving the whole panel resets all visited labels.
C-TOOLBAR-LABELS.ApprovalBasis: Owner explicitly requested cumulative label reveal for every such table/diagram toolbar on 2026-10-20: moving to a neighboring button must expand that button without collapsing the previous one, and all labels reset only after leaving the complete panel.

Goals.Goal: Accumulate visited labels independently within each table, Mermaid and Vega-Lite corner panel.
Keep prior button widths stable when traversing the panel; restore compact icons after leaving it.
Preserve keyboard labels, action routing, disabled/hidden controls, editing state and localized text.

Constraints.Constraint: No document, saved-state, undo, preference or persisted layout writes.
Share one local behavior across the existing expanding-inline-label factories. Do not turn unrelated floating tooltips or fixed viewer-header controls into expanding labels.
Keep C-TABLE-FOOTER separate and execute shared CSS changes sequentially. No version selection or publication.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No action redesign, new preference, floating-tooltip changes or viewer-header expansion.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Pointer traversal can reveal every available inline label in a table/diagram panel without collapsing earlier visited labels. Width never shrinks during that traversal, and the panel stays anchored.
Leaving the whole panel clears its visited-label state; entering a different panel starts compact. Focus-visible labels and keyboard action routing remain usable.
Both browser engines reproduce the old collapse before repair and pass after repair; source contracts, graph and verification projections describe the shared behavior.

AffectedAreas.Area: M-012 renderBlockToolbar/renderTableToolbar event hooks and shared CSS; block-toolbar units and table-toolbar-labels browser regressions covering all three corner-panel roles.
